# Source lists (editable)

These are **priorities for search**, not a guarantee that any author has written about any particular passage. The user retains control over which pastors are approved. Don't convert candidates into "trusted" by implication.

## Explicitly requested modern sermon sources (approved starting roster)

1. John Piper — original sermons and articles at https://www.desiringgod.org/ (distinguish Piper-authored texts from other Desiring God authors).
2. David Platt — original sermons at https://radical.net/ and church-hosted official archives.

Search each independently on the exact requested text. Check original transcript, title, sermon focus, date, author, and passage before selecting. **Do not use a message from a different preacher in their place** or pretend a series recap is a full exposition.

**Do not search all these by default**. Show the candidate list for future approval or add a candidate only if the user expressly requests breadth beyond the two-person roster.

## Commentary author pool — provisional theological fit, not user endorsement

Default center of gravity: evangelical, historically orthodox, Scripture-first biblical exposition with attention to gospel and literary/historical context. No presumption that every source speaks for the user's theological identity.

**Public-domain / historic candidates** (check exact edition and translation):
- Matthew Henry
- J. C. Ryle
- Thomas Watson
- Charles Spurgeon
- Alexander Maclaren
- John Calvin
- John Chrysostom
- Augustine of Hippo
- Keil and Delitzsch (Old Testament), where relevant
- Cambridge Bible for Schools and Colleges (relevant book/author)

**Modern evangelical scholarly candidates** (typically copyrighted; original text excerpts must stay very short):
- D. A. Carson
- R. T. France
- Douglas Moo
- Thomas Schreiner
- Craig Blomberg
- Leon Morris
- Craig Keener (sometimes a broader interpretive angle)
- Grant Osborne
- Gordon Fee

Use only authors relevant to the biblical book and passage. As appropriate, introduce a well-grounded alternative interpretation to expose a real exegetical question. Label it as an alternative, not a user's approved source.

## Research access points

- Original academic publisher and author's official commentary/book listing, if available.
- Christian Classics Ethereal Library (CCEL): https://ccel.org/
- Project Gutenberg: https://www.gutenberg.org/
- STEP Bible for text and language features: https://www.stepbible.org/
- Open-access institutional repositories and publisher-authorized chapter previews.
- Sermon transcript archives at original ministry/church websites; official videos/audio when transcript unavailable.
- User-provided Logos exports and personally owned manuscript notes, only when supplied or actually connected and accessible.
- User's own historical sermon manuscripts, if supplied/accessible, may be more directly relevant than a generic pastoral source.

Cross-check source dates and exact authors. Never assume access to user's licensed Logos library or quote content not retrieved.

## Maintainer decisions still useful (not prerequisites)

- Add/remove approved pastors, in preferred search order.
- Add preferred modern commentary series and denominational scholarly guardrails.
- Preferred Bible translation(s) and amount of original-language detail.
- Preferred final reading surface (Google Doc, Word, PDF) and source count.
